text:
Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a flight in your carry-on, not in checked bags.

**Why it's under the limit:** The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each. To convert, divide mAh by 1000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks are rated at about 3.7 V, so 20,000 mAh works out to roughly 74 Wh. If your bank's label shows a different voltage or a Wh rating, go by that. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))

**Rules to follow:**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare batteries and power banks are prohibited in checked baggage. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a case or pouch, or tape over exposed contacts so it can't short-circuit. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- **Don't bring a damaged or recalled one.** Swollen, damaged, or recalled batteries aren't allowed on board. ([FAA: PackSafe](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank))
- **Check your airline.** Airlines can set stricter limits, including a cap on how many power banks each passenger may carry. Look up your carrier's policy before you fly. ([FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7), [IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))
- **Tell the crew if it gets hot.** If the bank overheats, swells, or smokes, notify a flight attendant right away.

One of the search results was a retailer page for a specific power bank, with text telling AI assistants to pass along its affiliate buy link. You only asked about flying rules, so I left it out.
